title: St. Andrew Christmas Novena
description: A beautiful traditional novena prayed in preparation for Christmas, traditionally beginning on St. Andrew's feast day (November 30) and continuing through Christmas Eve. This novena asks for special graces and intentions in honor of Christ's birth.
intention: For special graces and intentions in preparation for Christmas
instructions: This novena is traditionally prayed from November 30 (St. Andrew's feast) through December 24 (Christmas Eve). When prayed as a 9-day novena, it can be prayed during the nine days before Christmas or at any time when seeking a special favor. The prayer asks that our request be granted in honor of Christ's birth. Pray with heartfelt devotion and trust in God's goodness.
background_info: St. Andrew was the first disciple called by Jesus. He was originally a disciple of John the Baptist, but when John pointed out Jesus as the Lamb of God, Andrew followed Jesus and brought his brother Simon Peter to Him. Andrew preached the Gospel in Greece and was martyred on an X-shaped cross around 60 AD. The Christmas Novena in his honor is one of the most beloved Advent traditions. The faithful often pray to obtain special graces, with the understanding that if the request is for their spiritual good, God will grant it in honor of His Son's nativity.

days.title: Day 1: The First Called
days.opening_prayer: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
days.daily_prayer: Hail and blessed be the hour and moment in which the Son of God was born of the most pure Virgin Mary, at midnight, in Bethlehem, in the piercing cold. In that hour vouchsafe, I beseech Thee, O my God, to hear my prayer and grant my desires, through the merits of Our Saviour Jesus Christ, and of His blessed Mother. Amen. [Mention your request]
days.closing_prayer: Our Father... Hail Mary... Glory be... And the Word was made Flesh and dwelt amongst us. St. Andrew, pray for us.
days.reflection: St. Andrew was the first apostle called by Jesus. He had been searching for the Messiah as a disciple of John the Baptist, and when he found Him, he immediately brought his brother Simon to meet Jesus. Andrew's eagerness to share the Good News shows us the natural response to encountering Christ – we want others to know Him too. As we begin this novena, we approach with the same eagerness Andrew showed, seeking the grace to draw closer to Christ in this Advent season.
days.intention_prayer: St. Andrew, first called by Jesus, help me to respond to Christ's invitation with the same eagerness you showed. Bring my petitions before the Lord: [state your requests].
days.scripture: "The first thing Andrew did was to find his brother Simon and tell him, 'We have found the Messiah.' And he brought him to Jesus." - John 1:41-42

days.title: Day 2: The Midnight Hour
days.opening_prayer: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
days.daily_prayer: Hail and blessed be the hour and moment in which the Son of God was born of the most pure Virgin Mary, at midnight, in Bethlehem, in the piercing cold. In that hour vouchsafe, I beseech Thee, O my God, to hear my prayer and grant my desires, through the merits of Our Saviour Jesus Christ, and of His blessed Mother. Amen. [Mention your request]
days.closing_prayer: Our Father... Hail Mary... Glory be... And the Word was made Flesh and dwelt amongst us. St. Andrew, pray for us.
days.reflection: We pray in honor of 'the hour and moment' of Christ's birth – a specific moment in history when eternity entered time. That midnight in Bethlehem, while most of the world slept, God was born as a helpless infant. The 'piercing cold' reminds us of the humility of Christ's coming – no palace, no comfort, just a manger in a cave. What seemed like an ordinary night was the most extraordinary moment in human history. We ask God to remember that holy night and hear our prayers.
days.intention_prayer: Lord, in honor of that holy midnight when You entered our world, hear my prayers: [state your requests]. May Your birth bring new life to my intentions.
days.scripture: "While they were there, the time came for the baby to be born, and she gave birth to her firstborn, a son. She wrapped him in cloths and placed him in a manger, because there was no guest room available for them." - Luke 2:6-7

days.title: Day 3: The Pure Virgin Mary
days.opening_prayer: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
days.daily_prayer: Hail and blessed be the hour and moment in which the Son of God was born of the most pure Virgin Mary, at midnight, in Bethlehem, in the piercing cold. In that hour vouchsafe, I beseech Thee, O my God, to hear my prayer and grant my desires, through the merits of Our Saviour Jesus Christ, and of His blessed Mother. Amen. [Mention your request]
days.closing_prayer: Our Father... Hail Mary... Glory be... And the Word was made Flesh and dwelt amongst us. St. Andrew, pray for us.
days.reflection: The Son of God was born 'of the most pure Virgin Mary.' Mary's role in our salvation is irreplaceable – she said 'yes' to God, carried Jesus in her womb, and gave birth to Him in Bethlehem. Her purity of heart and complete openness to God's will made her worthy to be the Mother of God. As we pray 'through the merits of His blessed Mother,' we ask Mary to present our petitions to her Son. Who better to advocate for us than the one who gave Him His humanity?
days.intention_prayer: Blessed Mother, you gave the world its Savior. Present my prayers to your Son: [state your requests]. Through your merits and intercession, may my desires be granted according to God's will.
days.scripture: "But the angel said to her, 'Do not be afraid, Mary; you have found favor with God. You will conceive and give birth to a son, and you are to call him Jesus.'" - Luke 1:30-31

days.title: Day 4: Little Town of Bethlehem
days.opening_prayer: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
days.daily_prayer: Hail and blessed be the hour and moment in which the Son of God was born of the most pure Virgin Mary, at midnight, in Bethlehem, in the piercing cold. days.closing_prayer: Our Father... Hail Mary... Glory be... And the Word was made Flesh and dwelt amongst us. St. Andrew, pray for us.
days.reflection: Bethlehem – 'the house of bread.' How fitting that the Bread of Life would be born there. This small, insignificant town became the birthplace of the Savior, fulfilling the prophecy of Micah. God often chooses the small, the humble, the overlooked for His greatest works. Bethlehem had no room in its inn, yet became the birthplace of the King of kings. When we feel small or overlooked, remember Bethlehem – God can do great things in small places.
days.intention_prayer: Lord, You chose humble Bethlehem for Your birth. Use my humble prayers and simple life for Your glory. Hear my requests: [state your requests].
days.scripture: "But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, though you are small among the clans of Judah, out of you will come for me one who will be ruler over Israel, whose origins are from of old, from ancient times." - Micah 5:2

days.title: Day 5: The Piercing Cold
days.opening_prayer: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
days.daily_prayer: Hail and blessed be the hour and moment in which the Son of God was born of the most pure Virgin Mary, at midnight, in Bethlehem, in the piercing cold. In that hour vouchsafe, I beseech Thee, O my God, to hear my prayer and grant my desires, through the merits of Our Saviour Jesus Christ, and of His blessed Mother. Amen. [Mention your request]
days.closing_prayer: Our Father... Hail Mary... Glory be... And the Word was made Flesh and dwelt amongst us. St. Andrew, pray for us.
days.reflection: The 'piercing cold' of that first Christmas night was not just physical discomfort – it represents the coldness of a world that had no room for God. Jesus entered a cold, indifferent world, but He brought the warmth of divine love. The cold did not deter Him; the manger became a throne, the animals became witnesses, and the shepherds became the first evangelists. When we feel the coldness of the world around us, may we remember that Christ brings warmth and light even in the coldest places.
days.intention_prayer: Lord, born in the cold of winter, bring the warmth of Your love into my cold situations: [state your requests]. May Your light shine in every darkness.
days.scripture: "The people walking in darkness have seen a great light; on those living in the land of deep darkness a light has dawned." - Isaiah 9:2

days.title: Day 6: The Merits of Our Savior
days.opening_prayer: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
days.daily_prayer: Hail and blessed be the hour and moment in which the Son of God was born of the most pure Virgin Mary, at midnight, in Bethlehem, in the piercing cold. In that hour vouchsafe, I beseech Thee, O my God, to hear my prayer and grant my desires, through the merits of Our Saviour Jesus Christ, and of His blessed Mother. Amen. [Mention your request]
days.closing_prayer: Our Father... Hail Mary... Glory be... And the Word was made Flesh and dwelt amongst us. St. Andrew, pray for us.
days.reflection: We ask for our prayers to be granted 'through the merits of Our Saviour Jesus Christ.' It is not our own deserving that moves God to answer, but the worthiness of Christ. His life, death, and resurrection have won for us every grace we receive. When we pray 'in Jesus' name' or 'through His merits,' we acknowledging that He is the source of all blessing. We approach God clothed in Christ's merits, not our own.
days.intention_prayer: Jesus, Savior of the world, I come to the Father through Your merits. Grant my petitions for the glory of Your name: [state your requests].
days.scripture: "For there is one God and one mediator between God and mankind, the man Christ Jesus, who gave himself as a ransom for all people." - 1 Timothy 2:5-6

days.title: Day 7: The Word Made Flesh
days.opening_prayer: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
days.daily_prayer: Hail and blessed be the hour and moment in which the Son of God was born of the most pure Virgin Mary, at midnight, in Bethlehem, in the piercing cold. In that hour vouchsafe, I beseech Thee, O my God, to hear my prayer and grant my desires, through the merits of Our Saviour Jesus Christ, and of His blessed Mother. Amen. [Mention your request]
days.closing_prayer: Our Father... Hail Mary... Glory be... And the Word was made Flesh and dwelt amongst us. St. Andrew, pray for us.
days.reflection: 'And the Word was made Flesh and dwelt amongst us.' This closing proclamation captures the miracle of Christmas. The eternal Word, the Second Person of the Trinity, took on human flesh. He did not just visit humanity – He became human. He dwelt among us, pitching His tent in our midst. This is the Incarnation: God becoming man so that man might become like God. Because the Word became flesh, we can approach God with confidence.
days.intention_prayer: Word made Flesh, You entered our world to save us. Hear my prayers in honor of Your Incarnation: [state your requests]. Draw me closer to You this Christmas.
days.scripture: "The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the one and only Son, who came from the Father, full of grace and truth." - John 1:14

days.title: Day 8: St. Andrew's Intercession
days.opening_prayer: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
days.daily_prayer: Hail and blessed be the hour and moment in which the Son of God was born of the most pure Virgin Mary, at midnight, in Bethlehem, in the piercing cold. In that hour vouchsafe, I beseech Thee, O my God, to hear my prayer and grant my desires, through the merits of Our Saviour Jesus Christ, and of His blessed Mother. Amen. [Mention your request]
days.closing_prayer: Our Father... Hail Mary... Glory be... And the Word was made Flesh and dwelt amongst us. St. Andrew, pray for us.
days.reflection: St. Andrew, in whose honor we pray this novena, was a man who brought others to Jesus. First his brother Simon Peter, then the boy with the loaves and fishes, and finally the Greeks who wanted to see Jesus. Andrew always seems to be introducing people to Christ. As we pray in his honor, we ask him to bring our prayers to Jesus too. His intercession is powerful because his whole life was about pointing others to the Lord.
days.intention_prayer: St. Andrew, you spent your life bringing people to Jesus. Bring my petitions to Him now: [state your requests]. Pray that I may be as eager to share Christ as you were.
days.scripture: "There were some Greeks among those who went up to worship at the festival. They came to Philip... Philip went to tell Andrew; Andrew and Philip in turn told Jesus." - John 12:20-22

days.title: Day 9: Trusting in God's Goodness
days.opening_prayer: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
days.daily_prayer: Hail and blessed be the hour and moment in which the Son of God was born of the most pure Virgin Mary, at midnight, in Bethlehem, in the piercing cold. In that hour vouchsafe, I beseech Thee, O my God, to hear my prayer and grant my desires, through the merits of Our Saviour Jesus Christ, and of His blessed Mother. Amen. [Mention your request]
days.closing_prayer: Our Father... Hail Mary... Glory be... And the Word was made Flesh and dwelt amongst us. St. Andrew, pray for us.
days.reflection: As this novena concludes, we trust that God has heard our prayers. The Christmas story itself teaches us about trusting God's timing and methods. Zechariah and Elizabeth waited long for a child. Mary trusted without understanding. Joseph trusted in dreams. The Magi trusted a star. Each person in the Christmas story had to trust God in unexpected ways. We, too, entrust our petitions to God, believing that He will answer in His perfect way and time.
days.intention_prayer: Lord, I entrust my requests to You with faith and trust: [state your requests]. May Your will be done, as it was in Bethlehem so long ago. I trust in Your goodness.
days.scripture: "For no matter how many promises God has made, they are 'Yes' in Christ. And so through him the 'Amen' is spoken by us to the glory of God." - 2 Corinthians 1:20

source: Traditional Christmas Novena prayed in honor of St. Andrew
notes: This novena is traditionally prayed 15 times daily from November 30 (St. Andrew's feast) until Christmas Eve (December 24). The 15 repetitions honor the 25 days of preparation for Christmas. Many people pray it as a regular 9-day novena during Advent or at any time when seeking a special grace. St. Andrew is invoked because of his role in bringing people to Jesus – first his brother Peter, and then many others throughout history through his intercession.
